subject: riotInterceptor
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: corporate riot-control interceptor with a water cannon and neon light bars.
Style: Cyberpunk 2077.
reasoning:
I'm planning out a single TypeScript module for a static armored interceptor truck model—boxy chassis, roof water cannon turret, neon light bars, wheels, and corp-logo textures—built with reusable helper functions for boxes, wheels, and light bars to keep the part count manageable yet detailed.

Working out exact dimensions and colors now, planning a gunmetal body with countershading and cyan/magenta/yellow neon accents, plus decal textures for hazard stripes, license plates, and "RIOT CONTROL" stencil text. Designing the body construction...

For the windshield I'll use a tilted box instead, computing the pitch angle from the slope between the two slope points and offsetting it slightly outward along the surface normal so it sits just above the body.

Now I'm adding details like dark-glass side windows with cyan reflections, armored wheel arches, a striped push-bar bumper, roof-mounted light bars with magenta/cyan glowing segments, yellow-white headlight slits, magenta taillights, and starting on a roof-mounted water cannon turret base.

Still adding vehicle details...

Setting overall height around 2.7, then building a mirrored body helper and decal/texture system for side panels and logos, making sure text reads correctly on both left and right sides when mirrored.

I'm sketching out a set of textures for the vehicle: a hexagonal "NEOGARD" logo, a stenciled unit designation, hazard stripes, a license plate, a glowing front grille, circuit-line panels, and a gradient water-level window — roughly six to seven decals total. For the body paint I'm planning a countershaded gunmetal finish with dirt accumulation lower down, paired with a white-and-graphite two-tone corporate color scheme.

Writing paint gradient code...
